column3: MT 65:1–2; the following verses of this psalm are MT +1. NASB sets the title in braces before verse 1. “To You silence is praise” is rendered “There will be silence before You, and praise.”
Close to the Hebrew; “all flesh” is rendered “all men.”
Close to the Hebrew; “You atone for them” is rendered “You forgive them.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the distant sea” is rendered “the farthest sea.”
NASB supplies “of the earth,” and renders “the goings out of morning and evening” as “the dawn and the sunset.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “the earth” at the end.
The Hebrew uses infinitive and imperative forms (“watering … soften it”); NASB renders them as statements, and “press down” as “settle.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the year of Your goodness” is rendered “the year with Your bounty,” and “tracks” as “paths.”
Close to the Hebrew; “pastures” is rendered “meadows.”
